overview: This file traces Japan’s petroleum policy from 1932 to 1934, from Soviet gasoline imports and price competition to the Petroleum Industry Law. Embassy reports, company correspondence, diplomatic cables, and translated legislation document foreign firms’ concerns about licensing, reserves, quotas, and prices. Records also cover oil development in Manchuria, alternative crude supplies, and proposals for coordinated diplomatic or export action.
interest: Translated laws, Diet hearings, company statistics, and diplomatic conversations reveal how oil security policy affected foreign firms.
